articles.title: Barrenetxea no podrá ir con la Selección y le sustituye De Frutos
articles.standfirst: El 7 realista estará varias semanas K.O.
articles.summary: El 7 realista estará varias semanas K.O.
articles.body: Ander Barrenetxea no se incorporará hoy a la concentración de España para los partidos ante Chequia e Inglaterra, después de que el extremo de la Real Sociedad se tuviera que marchar lesionado del partido ante el Rayo Vallecano en el minuto 70, ayudado por dos médicos del equipo donostriarra y entre lágrimas, lo que hace pensar que sufre un problema muscular lo suficientemente grave como para impedirle unirse al equipo de Luis de la Fuente. Su puesto en la convocatoria lo asume Jorge de Frutos, extremo del Rayo Vallecano, que se incorporará a la concentración de la Selección este lunes 9 de noviembre a partir de las 13 horas en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas. “Tenemos que esperar a las pruebas médicas, pero parece de los isquios”, decía Matarazzo al acabar el partido. “Ojalá que sea poco porque le necesitamos pronto”, añadió Remiro. ‘Barrene’, que estaba siendo uno de los mejores del partido y se encontraba en buena forma, notó el tirón después de ser clave en el primer gol del partido, asistiendo con un gran pase a Óskarsson para que se quedara solito ante Audero, al que batió. Pero le duró poco la alegría a la Real, porque acto seguido el extremo se tuvo que marchar lesionado, dejando su sitio a Ochieng. El 7 realista no fue el único que sufrió un problema así, porque en la parte final del partido el rayista Vertrouwd tuvo que ser reemplazado al poco de salir al césped de Anoeta. Luis de la Fuente ha premiado el gran momento de Jorge De Frutos con su convocatoria para el próximo parón de selecciones. Esta será la tercera convocatoria del de Navares de Enmedio con la Selección Española. Ya hizo su debut el 7 de septiembre de 2025 en la goleada por 0-6 ante Turquía en la que jugó algo más de 22 minutos. Beñat ya lo adelantó en la rueda de prensa previa al encuentro ante la Real. “Si el seleccionador no lo ha llevado, seguro que lo tendrá en su lista”. Efectivamente. De Frutos tendrá que luchar ahora por un puesto de cara a los encuentros ante República Checa (12 de noviembre) e Inglaterra (15 de noviembre).

articles.title: AP Top 25: Georgia moves to No. 1 after Notre Dame's win over Miami, Ohio State drops out of top 20
articles.summary: The Bulldogs demolished Ole Miss on Saturday.
articles.body:
Georgia is the new No. 1 team in the AP Top 25.

The Bulldogs took over the top spot after No. 1 Miami lost at Notre Dame on Saturday night. The Hurricanes fell to No. 5, behind Georgia, Utah, Notre Dame and UCLA.

Georgia blew out Ole Miss on Saturday and were the obvious choice to move up a spot. Utah beat BYU to move up to No. 2 , while UCLA won on the road at Minnesota.

Utah and UCLA are the only two remaining undefeated teams at the top level of college football.

The rest of the top 10 is filled out by Indiana, Alabama, Texas, Tennessee and Texas Tech. The Crimson Tide won at LSU on Saturday, while Tennessee had a dominant win over a Kentucky team that hadn't lost since Week 2 against Alabama.

Ohio State dropped all the way to No. 21 after losing at home to Oregon. The Buckeyes gave up 41 points in the loss and may be without a playoff path now that they have three losses.

Wake Forest is up to No. 11 as the second ACC team in the rankings. The Demon Deacons played FCS-level Merrimack on Saturday.

In Week 11, No. 2 Utah goes to No. 22 Arizona, No. 15 USC visits No. 6 Indiana and No. 8 Texas heads to No. 24 LSU. And we'll see on Tuesday night how much difference there is between the AP poll and the second set of College Football Playoff rankings. A week ago, Notre Dame was seven spots lower in the CFP rankings than it was in the AP Top 25.

articles.title: Bizarre & thrilling theatre as Carrick's Man Utd future still in limbo
articles.summary: It was a Premier League classic at Old Trafford but what as Man Utd's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa done to Michael Carrick's future?
articles.body:
After yet another breathless, chaotic, shambolic Old Trafford classic, Manchester United do not know whether to laugh or cry.

Their fans didn't, booing at some points, cheering at others.

Defender Diogo Dalot was singled out for gruesome treatment amid the second-half protests and songs of defiance as he was replaced by Patrick Dorgu in the 66th minute.

The players didn't, running away joyously to celebrate Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser that made it 4-4 against Aston Villa. They then applauded the supporters who stayed on despite the apparent hopelessness of the situation as the game entered injury-time with United trailing 4-2, presumably to vent their anger on a day when defeat seemed certain.

Manager Michael Carrick was in spiky mood when he was quizzed about his future by Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davison.

"That's not going to happen," he said, when asked if he was going to walk away.

"Will there?" Carrick then added, when it was suggested there would 'clearly be conversations' with United's hierarchy.

"You're telling me what you think," he responded.

"I'm quite clear what direction the club needs to go in. It's got to win games."

Sunday's ridiculous eight-goal thriller with Villa - a game in which the hosts fought back twice from two goals down - left United 18th in the table and in the Premier League drop zone.

As they enter the international break, they will spend more time in the relegation zone than they have done since 1986.

United have not won a league game since they beat Ipswich on August 30, have conceded 15 goals in their last five games and conceded inside two minutes in three of their last seven matches.

Three minutes and 40 seconds was the earliest they have ever trailed 2-0 in a Premier League game.

Up next is a trip to Anfield to play rivals Liverpool on 22 November.

On the positive side, United's players have not downed tools for their manager.

Somehow, despite being two goals down on three occasions in the last two games, they have emerged with a win and a draw.

Added to a creditable first-half display in a 2-0 loss at Chelsea on 31 October where they had Lisandro Martinez sent off, before which Carrick was backed to turn the current situation round, was that enough for Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family - and detached from this latest crazy day?

Was it enough for chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox who were at Old Trafford?

"On the one hand it's dreadful to give up four goals at home," former United skipper Roy Keane told Sky Sports. "But they kept going, so you have to give them a little bit of praise.

"In terms of the bigger picture it's that rollercoaster of watching Manchester United. When you turn up most weeks there really is the feeling of not knowing what you're going to get."

Former United striker Dion Dublin offered his own take on BBC Sport as he added: "There's only so many times you can do that because it's quite tiring, physically and mentally. The players today were walking around after the game like they had lost, even though they got a point."

Some of the post-match interviews by United players backed up that observation.

"I don't feel happy - we are in a bad situation," admitted Dorgu. "We need to fight together to get out of it.

"Everyone needs to look at themselves and ask if they are doing enough. We need to fight for the manager, for the club and get out of this together."

The situation has not been made easier by fan sentiment.

Lack of form on the pitch, combined with rising cost of ticket prices and a negative perception of how fans are being treated, has led to a negative reaction that is unprecedented in its ferocity since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

A banner was hung from the second tier of the Stretford End shortly before the teams came out to start the game. It read 'We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners'.

Full-back Dalot was jeered off the pitch when he was replaced by Dorgu, the catcalls replacing the cheers that greeted his number being shown.

Joshua Zirkzee, who scored United's third in the second minute of injury time, suffered similar treatment during a game against Newcastle almost two years ago. The Netherlands forward was still on the bench when Dalot arrived and offered his team-mate a consoling hug.

'We're just making it too difficult for ourselves'

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery was livid by his side's late capitulation, which cost him a first victory at Old Trafford.

Touted as a potential successor to Carrick, he regathered his composure after storming down the tunnel before the final whistle to assure United fans the club's results will improve.

"They have the capacity, power, players and everything to overcome this situation," said the Spaniard.

That is probably true. But from so many angles, the current position remained grim.

The Villa game was like a number so far this season - Everton away, Atletico Madrid away, Tottenham at home, Leeds away, Chelsea away - where either United have played well, or got themselves into winning positions in stoppage time and failed to secure victory.

Although the present situation can still be rectified, it now needs two lots of results to go Carrick's way for the table to look more positive. Yet how long will it be before it is accepted that such anticipated improvement is not going to materialise?

Can United afford to wait until the January window opens? Have they got the resources to spend in it when it does?

These are bound to feed into the thinking of Ratcliffe, the Glazers, Berrada and Wilcox as they consider the future; plus the attractiveness of potential replacements.

For now, Carrick is still looking to a future he is certain will be brighter than what he has just endured.

"There's more than enough," he said, when asked if he had seen enough to believe the current situation can be improved.

"Goals change games and you've got to deal with it. It's something we have to improve on drastically. We're just making it too difficult for ourselves at certain times.

"They (players) are switched on and concentrated, it's a variety of things. There's not a theme to it, apart from these one-off moments are catching us out at the moment."
authors: Simon Stone - Manchester United reporter at Old Trafford

articles.title: Joe Burrow overpowers Falcons as Bengals win in Madrid
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals got an outstanding performance from their star quarterback on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals got an outstanding performance from their star quarterback on Sunday.

Joe Burrow threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns as the Bengals beat the Atlanta Falcons, 34-17, at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain.

Ja'Marr Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown. Tee Higgins had five catches, including two scores.

The Falcons took a 7-0 lead as Michael Penix Jr. found Charlie Woerner for a 1-yard touchdown. The Bengals responded as Burrow threw a 47-yard touchdown pass to Chase to even the score at 7-7.

Nick Folk made a 31-yard field goal to give Atlanta a 10-7 advantage after one quarter.

Burrow's 1-yard touchdown run put Cincinnati ahead, 14-10. Higgins' 4-yard touchdown catch and Evan McPherson's 57-yard field goal extended it to 24-10 at halftime.

Bijan Robinson's 1-yard touchdown run cut the deficit to 24-17. But the Bengals answered as the Burrow found Higgins for an 8-yard touchdown to extend it to 31-17.

McPherson capped the scoring with a 43-yard field goal.

Burrow went 24-of-29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns. The Bengals also ran for 123 yards.

Cincinnati hosts Pittsburgh on Nov. 15 at Paycor Stadium for Sunday Night Football.

articles.title: Oregon Ducks' chances to make CFP skyrocket after win, per ESPN FPI
articles.summary: With the Oregon Ducks' win over the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday, their chances at making the College Football Playoff have skyrocketed.
articles.body:
Don't look now, but the Oregon Ducks season might be back on track, with expectations returning.

After a huge blowout win over the Ohio State Buckeyes in Columbus over the weekend, Dan Lanning's team kept its season alive, with real hopes of making the Big Ten Championship and potentially the College Football Playoff.

With three games left, Oregon has a decent chance to reach the Big Ten title game if it wins out, and even a chance to earn an at-large CFP bid when all is said and done. That much is reflected in the latest look at ESPN's Football Power Index.

Going into the weekend, Oregon had just a 4.2% chance to make the playoff, but that number skyrocketed to 24.9% after the win in Columbus. Nothing is possible unless the Ducks win their final three games, but at this point, it's reasonable to say there is a chance.

Here's a look at the new ESPN FPI numbers and what they mean for the Ducks.

Oregon Percent Chance to Win, Per ESPN FPI: 85.9%

Analysis: What looked like a very tough game at the start of the year has really lost some of its luster. Oregon is starting to click at the right time, while Michigan is watching the wheels fall off. After a loss to the Michigan State Spartans over the weekend, the Kyle Whittingham era may be headed for a quick end, as the Ducks are now double-digit favorites in this game at home.

Oregon Percent Chance to Win, Per ESPN FPI: 84.4%

Analysis: Despite the Spartans' big win over Michigan over the weekend, it doesn't all of a sudden make them a major threat in this game. While it is a road game on a short week for Oregon, I still think they will be favored by double digits and should be able to come out on top should they play with the level of success that we've seen over the past couple of weeks.

Oregon Percent Chance to Win, Per ESPN FPI: 86.7%

Analysis: Washington may not be playing for much in this game, but Oregon could potentially be trying to keep its season alive, whether that be in the race for a spot in the Big Ten Championship game or an at-large bid into the College Football Playoff. The Huskies have been struggling mightily this season, so the Ducks should be favored by quite a bit going into this game.

Percent Chance to Make College Football Playoff: 24.9%

Percent Chance to Make National Championship: 2.0%

Percent Chance to Win National Championship: 0.8%
